hub.intro: Airlines, lessors and investors, MROs and government operators each meet the same engine from a different side. Start with yours.

industries.name: Airlines
industries.seoTitle: Engine shop visit management for airlines | Flight Hour Solution
industries.metaDescription: Independent shop visit management, workscope and removal planning, engine data review and MRO contract support for airline powerplant teams. Zug, Switzerland.
industries.audience: For VPs Technical, heads of powerplant, engine fleet managers, CAMO leads and procurement teams who own fleet availability and the engine budget.
industries.situation: Engines are the largest and fastest-growing segment of aircraft maintenance. Against pre-pandemic levels, turnaround times are up 35 per cent or more on legacy engines and 150 per cent or more on new-generation types, and slot waits are two to three months longer, up to six. A lean powerplant team cannot sit in every shop. We fill that gap.

whatWeDo.title: An extra pair of hands at the shop
whatWeDo.text: Full or overview shop visit management from pre-induction to redelivery: workscope review, dirty condition and table inspection, test cell overview and invoice review. We work alongside your powerplant team and report to it.

whatWeDo.title: Removal timing and the workscope
whatWeDo.text: Removal planning against LLP limits, EGT margin and slot lead times, then a workscope that fits the lease, the budget and the engine's next run, including durability kit decisions on LEAP.

whatWeDo.title: A second read of your engine data
whatWeDo.text: Independent review of ECM and EHM trends, borescope video and test cell results, so the removal decision is timed by you rather than by whoever sells the shop visit.

whatWeDo.title: Contracts and invoices, on your side
whatWeDo.text: Engine overhaul and repair contract negotiation, warranty management and line-by-line invoice review, whether you buy maintenance by the flight hour or by time and material.

whatWeDo.title: Keeping the judgement in the team
whatWeDo.text: Workshops for powerplant, CAMO and procurement staff on reading a workscope, a findings report and an invoice, built from the methods we use on engagements.

industries.name: Lessors and investors
industries.seoTitle: Engine technical advisor for lessors and investors | Flight Hour Solution
industries.metaDescription: Lease return support, maintenance reserve and claim analysis, back-to-birth records audits and technical due diligence for lessors, lenders and investors.
industries.audience: For technical asset managers, heads of engines and the lenders, funds, servicers and insurers who carry the residual value risk on engines and aircraft.
industries.situation: At the end of a lease, the reserve clause and the redelivery conditions are where multi-million-dollar disputes start. Early shop visits and unexpected module swaps are testing lease language that never anticipated them, and lenders scrutinise engine status more closely than they used to. Value sits in the records, the LLPs and the next shop visit.

whatWeDo.title: Redelivery, reserves and records
whatWeDo.text: Redelivery management for the lessee or acceptance for the lessor, maintenance reserve calculations and claim analysis, and LLP back-to-birth trace audits. We act for one side, or between the two, and say which.

whatWeDo.title: The shop visit under your lease
whatWeDo.text: When a lessee's engine goes to the shop mid-lease or before return: workscope approval against the lease terms, table inspection attendance, test cell overview and invoice review, so the engine comes back in the condition the lease describes.

whatWeDo.title: Due diligence before money moves
whatWeDo.text: Records audits back to birth, maintenance status and cost forecasts, the engine exposure of a whole portfolio and teardown valuations, for acquisitions, financings, ABS closings and engine-only deals.

whatWeDo.title: Watching the portfolio between events
whatWeDo.text: Fleet ECM and EHM monitoring programmes and on-wing performance reviews across leased engines, so an early removal is seen coming and raised with the lessee, not reported after the fact.

whatWeDo.title: Lease and purchase contracts
whatWeDo.text: Lease contract and engine purchase negotiation support, insurance claims support and warranty management, with return and reserve clauses that anticipate early shop visits and module swaps.

industries.name: MROs
industries.seoTitle: Independent support for engine MROs and overhaul shops | Flight Hour Solution
industries.metaDescription: Material and scrap review, findings and records review, new engine type induction support and training for independent and airline-affiliated engine shops.
industries.audience: For heads of engine shops, commercial directors and customer support engineers at independent and airline-affiliated MROs who want fewer disputes and better-run inductions.
industries.situation: Cumulative engine MRO demand exceeds supply by nearly 17 per cent through the end of the decade and OEM parts demand by 10 to 20 per cent. Slots are contested, findings are questioned and invoices are read line by line. Our shop visit management is built for airlines and lessors, so we know what a customer will accept.

whatWeDo.title: Material strategy and scrap review
whatWeDo.text: Material sourcing support, scrap rate analysis and material value extraction, and a used serviceable material policy for a market in which teardown harvesting runs five times below pre-2020 levels.

whatWeDo.title: Findings and records that hold
whatWeDo.text: Table inspection findings, test cell results and post-shop visit documentation reviewed against the workscope before they reach the customer, so the record holds when the invoice is questioned.

whatWeDo.title: Induction readiness for a new type
whatWeDo.text: Workscope compilation and review for an engine type new to the shop, durability kit embodiment decisions on LEAP, and industry best practice advice while the induction plan is built.

whatWeDo.title: Training for customer-facing engineers
whatWeDo.text: Workshops for customer support and shop engineers on how airlines and lessors read a workscope, a findings report and an invoice, built from the way we run shop visits for airlines and lessors and the team's experience in engine shops and airline engineering.

industries.name: Government and military
industries.seoTitle: Engine sustainment support for government and military fleets | Flight Hour Solution
industries.metaDescription: Independent oversight of military engine shop visits, sole-source contract support, maintenance forecasting and training for defence and government fleets.
industries.audience: For programme managers, heads of sustainment, logistics commands and procurement officers who answer for the availability and life-cycle cost of a government fleet.
industries.situation: Military MRO is growing about ten times faster than in the previous decade, with engines leading, and a doubling of European defence spending could bring shortages of parts, production capacity and skilled labour. Where the engine OEM is the only overhaul supplier, workscope, cost and turnaround are hard to challenge from inside the programme. Independent oversight makes them defensible.

whatWeDo.title: Oversight of the engine sustainment contract
whatWeDo.text: Full shop visit management for military engines, borescope and test cell analysis for operational readiness, and post-shop visit documentation audits and performance reviews, reported to the programme office rather than to the supplier.

whatWeDo.title: Negotiating with a sole supplier
whatWeDo.text: Engine overhaul and repair contract negotiation, purchase, lease and insurance claims support and warranty management, bringing an outside view of workscope, cost and turnaround into a negotiation that otherwise has one side's numbers.

whatWeDo.title: Life-cycle cost and maintenance forecasting
whatWeDo.text: Maintenance cost forecasting, removal planning and fleet shop visit planning for the programme, so readiness targets and budget lines rest on the same set of numbers.

whatWeDo.title: Your own read of the engine data
whatWeDo.text: An independent read of ECM and EHM trends, borescope video and on-wing performance, for fleets where the supplier's monitoring is otherwise the only view and data sovereignty matters.

whatWeDo.title: Knowledge transfer to the programme team
whatWeDo.text: Training for programme, logistics and procurement staff on shop visits, workscopes and invoices, so the judgement stays inside the service when people rotate out.
